claims.label: CHOSEN
claims.text: The restaurant owner and patio staff should begin a voluntary soft close at 11:45pm by lowering music and guiding conversations indoors; compare aggregated 311 complaints from 10pm to 1am before and after the change, with the restaurant and its workers carrying the primary coordination burden.

claims.label: CHOSEN
claims.text: Recreation-center staff should stagger program endings and ask teenagers to leave in small groups during a posted departure window; track weekly aggregated complaints about departures, with center staff and participating teens carrying the primary scheduling and cooperation burden.

claims.label: CHOSEN
claims.text: The neighborhood association should distribute voluntary pickup instructions directing rideshare drivers to wait quietly at the existing alley entrance and avoid repeated horn use; use voluntary resident surveys and aggregated 311 counts to measure alley noise, with association volunteers and rideshare users carrying the primary communication burden.

claims.label: CHOSEN
claims.text: The drummer should adopt a voluntary practice schedule that ends the loudest practice before 10pm and notify nearby neighbors of the general schedule; compare anonymous survey reports of drum disturbance over 90 days, with the drummer carrying the primary accommodation burden.

claims.label: CHOSEN
claims.text: The association should fund modest sound-dampening improvements for the restaurant patio and recreation-center exit using the one-time budget; compare the number of nighttime complaints before and after installation, with the association bearing the primary financial burden.

claims.label: CHOSEN
claims.text: Restaurant and recreation-center managers should train workers to use a consistent quiet-closing script that asks patrons to lower voices and leave calmly; review monthly aggregated 311 trends and voluntary worker feedback, with managers and their staff carrying the primary training burden.

claims.label: CHOSEN
claims.text: The association should create a voluntary resident and business liaison group that meets twice during the 90-day period to resolve recurring nighttime friction; measure whether repeat complaints decline in the following month, with association volunteers and participating stakeholders carrying the primary meeting burden.

claims.label: FORCED
claims.text: The association must use only existing 311 data, voluntary surveys, and published business hours for evaluation and must not add surveillance or audio recording; report only aggregate complaint trends, with the association carrying the primary recordkeeping burden.

claims.label: FORCED
claims.text: Any neighborhood rule must preserve legitimate nighttime restaurant, recreation-center, rideshare, and drum activity without banning one activity outright or requiring residents to seek advance permission; assess success through complaint trends within 90 days, with the rule designers carrying the primary design burden.

claims.label: FORCED
claims.text: The association must avoid publishing complaint locations or identities and must not place the primary cost or volunteer burden on renters, teenagers, or low-wage workers; review participation and complaint feedback in aggregate, with the association carrying the primary privacy and equity burden.
